ghi_chu: NC-N2P · danh sách LỖI THỜI ĐẠI CẤM (mục 1(c)) — dùng NGUYÊN VĂN trong đề bài của bộ soi (vision_kiem.py). Phần 'chung' áp mọi cảnh trước 1850; phần 't4_1666' áp riêng London 1666; phần 'ai_da_bia' là các loại AI đã bịa ở NC-V2V/NC-V2V3/PT/ĐÓNG-GÓI.
chung: motor vehicles of any kind: cars, trucks, buses, motorcycles, tractors, trains, trams, rail tracks
aircraft of any kind: aeroplanes, helicopters, airships, drones, contrails; airfields, runways, aprons, hangars
steam or motor ships: funnels, smokestacks, paddle wheels, steel hulls, container ships, cargo ships, ferries, cruise ships, modern yachts, modern buoys
electric or gas lighting: street lamps on poles, searchlights, floodlights, neon, illuminated windows in rows, traffic lights
power or telephone poles and wires, pylons, antennas, satellite dishes, wind turbines, cranes of steel
modern materials and surfaces: asphalt, road markings, concrete blocks, steel-and-glass buildings, corrugated metal, plastic, tarpaulins in bright synthetic colours, chain-link or metal fences

modern buildings and structures: stadiums or arenas with stands, sports fields with markings, high-rise or multi-storey blocks of modern type, factories with chimneys, gasometers, lighthouses of modern type, bridges of iron or steel, modern harbour walls with bollards

modern clothing: jeans, t-shirts, hoodies, sneakers, baseball caps, top hats (1790s+), tricorn hats are borderline for 1666 (common only from the 1690s), high-visibility clothing, modern uniforms (khaki, camouflage, helmets of modern type)
modern weapons and military objects: rifles with bayonets of modern type, machine guns, tanks, armoured vehicles, artillery on rubber wheels
writing in the scene: any letters, numbers, shop signs, posters, logos, watermarks, street name plates
modern plants and landscaping: lawns with mowing stripes, ornamental planters, palm trees imported in rows
t4_1666: the Monument column near Pudding Lane (begun 1671, finished 1677)
St Paul's Cathedral with a DOME (Wren's cathedral, begun 1675, topped out 1708); in 1666 Old St Paul's had a long Gothic nave and a square tower with NO spire (spire lost 1561)
Wren-style white Portland-stone church steeples and towers in the City (all rebuilt after 1670)
the two western towers of Westminster Abbey (built in the 1740s)
Tower Bridge (1894), the present London Bridge, Blackfriars, Westminster or Southwark bridges; London Bridge in 1666 is the medieval bridge with houses on it
the Houses of Parliament / Big Ben clock tower (1840s-1870)
the Globe theatre on Bankside (pulled down 1644-45)
Thames embankments with stone river walls and promenades (1860s+); in 1666 the river edge is wharves, stairs and houses
Georgian brick terraces with sash windows, regular facades and parapets (post-fire rebuilding 1667+ and 18th c.); sash windows (1670s+)
street lamps of any kind on poles; public street lighting only from the late 17th century
fire engines with ladders, hoses, brass or red-painted modern fire engines, firefighters in helmets
the second Royal Exchange (1669) or the third (1844)
ai_da_bia: aircraft parked on an apron (NC-V2V c2-a)
flags of later design, e.g. Union Flag of 1801 with the saltire of St Patrick in a pre-1801 scene (PT §15)
lamps turned into flags or flags turned into lamps (ĐÓNG-GÓI v2 F2)
fires and smoke columns invented in streets or on the water (NC-V2V c1, c2-a)
stone buildings, cliffs and sailing ships invented (NC-V2V c4B-c)
added architectural details: cornices, carved ledges, doors, balconies (ĐÓNG-GÓI v2 F4, BIBLE §11.3)
land turned into sea or sea into sand (NC-V2V3 §4b)
